Mara’s eyes went directly to Livia Sloane, who was standing just outside the door, waiting for the man to finish what he was saying before they came inside. He was a tall and stately man, wearing a dark suit and carrying an iPad under one arm; Livia wore the same sort of loose white linen dress she’d worn before. Her gaze was fixed on Mara, level and friendly.

Then Adrian Voss spoke; Mara’s attention switched to him. He had a low voice that resonated deeply in his chest and seemed to hang in the air for a while, a sound that made it easy for a listener to imagine he meant exactly what he said. It was the same voice from the phone, from the interview in the hotel room.
“—we have a short reading session together,” he was saying as Livia’s companion pulled open the door and let them both through. “But only as long as it needs to be, of course; we’re not trying to force you or rush you.”

Adrian’s eyes met Mara’s, dark in his olive skin and still so focused on her that they seemed to almost glow, as though she were the only person he saw. He lifted both hands away from his sides to gesture toward Jonah, who had stayed very still since the moment Mara first set her eyes on him.
“You’ve met Jonah already, I see. But you don’t know Livia yet.” Adrian smiled warmly at her and turned his attention back to Mara. “She works here—she’s one of our most skilled observers.”

Mara looked from Adrian to Livia, who nodded. She felt very aware of Jonah at her side, though he still didn’t say a word—and she realized she hadn’t heard him introduce himself to Adrian or Livia earlier. His presence was solid in the room as they talked together, but his words were somehow nonexistent.

“She’s not the only one we have,” Adrian said, “but I want you to meet her right now.” He gestured once more toward Livia, who nodded again and smiled. She was standing behind him, just far enough away that it felt like she might come forward and hug him any moment—but then Adrian spoke again.
“Livia is a very experienced reader,” he said. “She’ll be able to tell us all how we’re doing together.”

He gestured toward the two of them, at their standing in this small room with Jonah beside them. They were so close now that Mara could feel the heat radiating off his skin through her shirt, almost as though it was touching him. He seemed to be holding something in his right hand, but she couldn’t tell what it was.
Adrian turned back toward Livia Sloane. “Thank you so much for coming,” he said to her, and held out one arm to embrace her.
Livia reached back with both arms and kissed him on either cheek before releasing her grip. “You’re welcome,” she whispered in his ear as they separated, then stepped away from him a few inches. “I’m happy to be here.”
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

Jonah had very warm palms; there was calloused skin on his right one, around the fingers but not the thumb. He didn’t look nervous, but his grip was firm and his smile seemed a little brittle, as though he were trying to keep hold of something.
Then his grip loosened. “Um—” His eyes flickered past Mara toward the open door. A low voice was speaking out in the hall—a man’s voice, saying something she couldn’t quite catch, and another voice replying in a woman’s light tone. She heard a small click and knew they would be in the room any moment now.

“I’m Mara,” she said into the silence.
“Mara,” Jonah repeated, letting go of her hand at last. “Hi. segment:
Adrian. And Livia.
Jonah nodded at them both in quick succession, still keeping himself turned toward Mara’s shoulder and smiling. He said something about wanting to wash up, then walked back to the couch to get a glass and some kind of bottled water. He opened it, took a sip, then walked over to a cluster of tall potted plants against the wall—

“Hi,” Livia greeted them with a wave. Mara barely registered her expression.
Then again: “Hi, Mara.”
The white-haired woman looked younger than Mara had expected, her face small and heart-shaped. She was wearing a long gray dress that pooled around her feet like water, with silver beads sewn in patterns across her shoulder and throat. Her eyes were brown, the same shade as her hair, but framed by so many thick lashes that they seemed to gleam with an inner light.

“Hi,” Mara said. She offered no wave in return.
The woman seemed not to notice this slight. She walked closer and took Mara’s hand again, her gaze now fixed on it. Mara didn’t know what to do with the contact; there was no polite way to withdraw, but it felt like the gesture should have some purpose. The woman’s eyes flicked up at Adrian briefly, who was standing a few feet away watching them both—

She heard the soft thud of Jonah’s glass being set back on the table, and felt it vibrate through her bones as Livia released her hand at last. Mara watched her go back to Adrian; they continued speaking quietly as though she wasn’t there.
She stood very still for a moment more, taking in their poses and movements—the way Livia leaned forward while she talked to Adrian, the slight tilt of her head toward his shoulder—

The group had come together around a low coffee table at the far end of the room; Mara sat down on one side while Adrian took up position facing her across from Livia, who settled herself on another couch. Jonah came in at that moment, dressed in jeans and a pale blue shirt with sleeves rolled to his elbows—

“You look good,” he said as he handed Mara a glass full of red wine.
She smiled at him and took it, placing the glass carefully on the table before turning her attention back to Adrian and Livia, who were watching her expectantly. Livia had unbuttoned the top half of her dress, leaving bare the smooth curves of her shoulders beneath a cloud of fine white hair, which she’d taken care to brush to one side as though it were an elegant shawl. She seemed very much in control—

“So,” said Adrian, “I understand that you don’t want to talk about yourself today.”
